title: The high-velocity tail: escape velocity, non-Maxwellian tails and the reach of inelastic dark matter at LZ
question: How do v_esc (500-600), v0 (220-250), rho0 (0.3-0.5) and the tail shape (sharp vs Lisanti k=1-3 vs SHM++ Sausage) change delta_max(248 keV), the O1 inelastic in-ROI rate at delta=250-380 keV, the coupling inferred from one event, and P007's Higgsino window?
headline_result: delta_max moves 0.82 keV per km/s of v_max (312-443 keV at 1 TeV over the envelope); Gaia-range halo parameters spread the LZ inelastic rate by 0.7/1.5/3.6 dex at delta=300/350/380 keV (1 TeV) and shift the Higgsino delta(N=1)=366 keV by -17..+11 keV (window 341-391); Lisanti k=2-3 tails lower the rate by 1e2-1e5 (window 317/278 keV); the anisotropic Sausage reduces the tail by 20%; halo spread exceeds x10 for delta > 291/324/343 keV (400/1000/4000 GeV) and x10 already at delta~110 keV if the tail form is free
